newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares at all-time low on Dadas woes.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares at all-time low on Dadas woes.

text.p: Slovenian shares slipped 0.22 percent on Tuesday to record an all-time low for the second day in a row with investors rattled by the shroud of mystery surrounding the fate of financial consultancy Dadas.
On Monday, the index dropped five percent following a 53.05 percent fall in Dadas on rumours the company's brokerage may be banned from trading while the consultancy itself may face bankruptcy.
The Ljubljana bourse today suspended trading in Dadas shares due to Monday's freefall and until the company explains whether there were any changes in its business to warrant such a sell-off.

"Today was marked by calmness after yesterday's black Monday. Although further large falls are unlikely -- as prices are considered to be very low already -- sentiment is so bearish that prices could fall further," one broker said.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 1.95 points to 891.93.
* Eight shares fell and six rose, while nine were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 21.2 million tolars from 72.5 million.
* Pharmaceutical trading company Salus had the highest turnover, falling 2.5 percent to 12,713 tolars on volume of 320 shares for total turnover of 4.1 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner. Its shares fell 3.89 percent to 15,632 on volume of 30 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars.
* Drug company Lek was the top gainer, rising 2.24 percent to 13,695 on volume of 38 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
